channel.title: Israel National News Flashes
channel.description: Latest news flashes from Israel National News

item.title: From Hamas captivity to Nobel Peace Prize bid: Amit Soussana's story
item.description: Former hostage Amit Soussana, who courageously exposed Hamas's sexual violence, is set to be nominated for the 2027 Nobel Peace Prize in recognition of her global advocacy for survivors.

item.title: Severe flu complication: Woman, 47, hospitalized in critical condition
item.description: A 47-year-old woman with no known underlying medical conditions was hospitalized in critical condition after contracting influenza A. She is sedated and connected to an ECMO machine.

item.title: Don't draft, disband: Foe of growing religious influence wants fewer haredim in IDF
item.description: Attorney Yair Nehorai, a leading opponent of growing religious influence, calls for ending efforts to draft haredim and disbanding the IDF's haredi units. He tells Arutz Sheva why he believes mass enlistment threatens Israel's liberal character.

item.title: "Bring about real change": Maj. (res.) Yitzhaki Glick's plan to resolve the draft issue
item.description: In an Arutz Sheva studio interview, Maj. (res.) Yitzhaki Glick, an attorney, says Bismuth's and Liberman's draft plans fall short. He proposes universal service, a small Torah study quota and a Zionist government not reliant on haredi parties.

item.title: Israeli doctors help 13-year-old Syrian Druze girl walk again
item.description: A 13-year-old Syrian Druze girl regained her ability to walk following surgery in Israel, 'A child is a child, regardless of where she was born,' says Prof. Salman Zarka, director of Ziv Medical Center.

item.title: Hundreds of kilograms of tobacco hidden in blankets and winter clothing bound for Gaza
item.description: An attempt to smuggle hundreds of kilograms of tobacco into Gaza was foiled at Kerem Shalom. It was hidden in sacks among winter items and sewn into blankets. COGAT froze aid entry permits for the Israeli company and trader involved.

item.title: Netanyahu confidant reveals what worries the prime minister
item.description: Attorney Lior Katzav, who spoke with Netanyahu, discusses concerns over the formation of an Eisenkot-led government, warns the haredi parties and addresses the possibility of a rotation agreement with Bennett.

item.title: Uzi Dayan warns: We are in the midst of World War III
item.description: Former IDF Deputy Chief of Staff Maj. Gen. (res.) Uzi Dayan speaks to Hadar Miller in the Arutz Sheva studio about the October 7 failure, Israel's survival, a unity government and his journey toward religious observance and daily Talmud study.

item.description: Political leaders paid tribute to former minister Rabbi Yitzhak Levy, remembering his unwavering principles, humility, and lifelong dedication to Torah, the Land of Israel, and the Jewish people.

item.title: 38-year-old man was seriously injured in a wild boar attack in Haifa
item.description: A 38-year-old man was seriously injured after being attacked by a wild boar in Haifa. MDA teams evacuated him to Bnei Zion Hospital in serious and unstable condition, with bruises on his limbs.

item.title: British synagogues cancel appearances by Rabbi Leo Dee over political remarks
item.description: Two British synagogues cancel scheduled appearances by Rabbi Leo Dee, whose wife and daughters were murdered by terrorists, reportedly over concerns about his remarks on Gaza and comparisons to Nazi-era antisemitism.

item.title: What did Rabbi Goren rule? His son and Temple Mount yeshiva head dispute ascent routes
item.description: Rami Goren told Arutz Sheva's podcast his father opposed today's Temple Mount routes. Yeshiva head Rabbi Elisha Wolfson says Goren permitted entry to large areas and that a letter he published in 5746 (1985-86) supports this view.

item.title: Ebola in Israe? Man who returned from Congo quarantined
item.description:
The Ministry of Health announced that a person who returned from the Democratic Republic of Congo and developed symptoms that raise suspicion of Ebola was referred for examination and treatment under isolation conditions at Ichilov Hospital.
The ministry emphasizes that at this stage this is only a suspicion, and that epidemiological tests and investigations are being conducted to identify contacts.

item.title: Woman hit by train at Ben Gurion Airport station; disruptions to train traffic
item.description:
A person who entered the track area at Ben Gurion Airport station in violation of instructions was hit by a passing train.
Emergency and rescue teams are working at the scene, and due to the incident, there are delays and changes to train traffic in the area.

item.title: Chief Rabbi blasts European leaders over silence on antisemitism
item.description: Rabbi Pinchas Goldschmidt warns that Jewish communities are becoming increasingly isolated across Europe. 'A Europe where a Jew questions his future is Europe’s failure,' says Albanian Prime Minister Edi Rama.

item.title: Nova survivor rushes burglar: "I thought only of my children; the lioness in me came out"
item.description: Miri Ben Shoshan, 35, a Nova survivor, awoke to a burglar as her two children slept. She grabbed his belt before he fled via scaffolding. She told Arutz Sheva of her fear, resurfacing trauma and the police decision to close the case.
